content.title: About
content.content: Pecan pie is a dessert featuring a flaky crust filled with a sweet mixture of ground pecans, sugar, butter, and eggs. The pecan (Carya illinoinensis) is a North American nut known for its buttery flavor and rich aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pecans belong to the hickory family and are more closely related to oak than to typical nuts.
In the United States, pecans are considered the national nut; Texas hosts an annual "Pecan Fest".
Pecan trees can live over 300 years and begin producing nuts after about 30 years.
The caramel sauce often used in the filling is traditionally made from molasses, a by‑product of sugarcane processing.
Pecans are high in antioxidants, especially flavonoids and phenolic acids.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Pecans provide vitamin E and polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Most of the fat in pecans is monounsaturated, which supports heart health.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in pecans promotes healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pecans contain thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pecans, ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Pecan pie is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The filling often contains a lot of sugar, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Pecans contain oxalates that may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pecan pie is served as a dessert with tea or coffee. Slice into portions and enjoy warm or chilled. Leftover pieces store well in the refrigerator.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pie in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 3 months. Allow it to come to room temperature before serving.
